17 October 2026 · first working implementation

Stickers, Colour Mix and Replace Colour

These tools use the existing local, nondestructive photo pipeline. Originals remain untouched. Existing project records receive neutral defaults for the new fields. This is a functioning first implementation, not a claim of physical-device or professional garment-selection validation.

Where to find them

  • Editor → Annotate → Stickers: 60 original vector catalogue entries: 12 dress-up accessories, 24 greetings and 24 decorations including colour variants. Move, resize, rotate, flip, duplicate, change opacity or delete in the annotation draft. Apply commits the draft; Cancel discards it. GIF annotation controls also have Add Sticker and existing frame visibility settings.
  • Editor → Adjust → All Adjustments: Colour adds Vibrance and Tint. Colour Mix provides eight colour bands with Hue (±60°), Saturation and Lightness (±100%) and per-band reset. Changes use field-specific patches, including in Batch Edit. Reset Light & Colour preserves creative filters and Auto Enhance.
  • Editor → Adjust → All Adjustments → Replace Colour: trace an area, sample the original colour, choose a replacement, then refine range, strength and edge softness. Pinch or use View Zoom, and enable Pan to move a zoomed view. Apply targets the captured photo only; stale drafts are refused. Existing areas can be reopened, adjusted or individually removed.

Rendering and compatibility

Global colour adjustments remain in the existing base-adjustment stage. Colour Mix and replacement kernels explicitly match sRGB values into and out of the context working space, preserving the established context for old edits. Local replacements run after framing/canvas and creative looks, before retouch, protective masks, annotations and watermarks. Matching uses hue/saturation across fabric shadows; replacement changes hue/saturation and relative HSL lightness rather than painting a flat fill. Preview and export share the same implementation.

Sticker IDs are versioned v1 catalogue IDs, with original Core Graphics paths and Core Text lettering, not copied packs or emoji artwork. The bundled artwork and IDs must remain available for saved edits. Unavailable stickers fail visibly. Projects persist semantic instructions, not GPU objects. Whole-object sticker opacity uses a transparency layer so overlapping artwork does not accumulate opacity.

Native captures

Hosted native views using generated demo photos. Recolouring outlines were set by the test fixture; these captures do not prove physical tracing accuracy. Mac captures show view content and can omit native window/toolbars. The demo polygon intentionally covers a selected portion, not automatic identification of the entire shirt. Component-only Colour Mix captures are not full-editor space comparisons.

Verification

Final Core run: 139 tests executed, one opt-in release-performance test skipped, zero failures. The last native targeted runs each passed nine tests, including the new panels and per-photo draft protections.

Core tests cover legacy decoding, sparse patches, transparency, selected/unselected pixel behaviour, fabric lightness, colour-space agreement, all 60 sticker renderers, sticker flip/opacity, unavailable stickers, configuration restoration, real preview/export and unchanged source bytes. Native tests cover single-photo scope, Undo/Redo, stale-draft rejection and the new panels, including large-text sticker browsing.

The full suites ran before the last presentation/zoom refinements; the final targeted runs built those refinements on each platform. Mobile full suites each skip the opt-in hardware performance measurement and the Photos permission integration check. Core skips the opt-in release performance measurement. Exact logs are recorded in the adjacent JSON manifest.

Limits and next validation

  • No automatic face placement, garment recognition, object segmentation or brush Add/Erase refinement. Areas are traced manually and can be retraced.
  • No HDR development: Colour Mix and Replace Colour reject detected HDR sources. Basic existing adjustments retain their established behaviour.
  • Black, white, patterned and translucent fabric, hair edges and reflected light require careful review; a colour change cannot recreate missing detail.
  • Up to 16 replacement areas per photo. Coverage rasterisation is capped at a 2048-pixel long edge, then scaled and feathered in output coordinates. This bounds coverage buffers but can limit extremely fine edges in large exports.
  • Physical-device tracing, pinch/Pencil arbitration, VoiceOver, keyboard workflow, low-memory behaviour and release performance remain to be verified. No M1 timing targets or device performance claims are made.
  • Sticker lettering uses fixed phrases in this catalogue; normal text annotations remain available for custom captions.

No signing changes, new dependencies, uploads, accounts, commits or pushes were introduced by this implementation.
